name: Tim O'Reilly
moniker: Publisher Who Named Web 2.0 and the Open Source Movement
quick_facts: Founded O'Reilly Media, publisher of technical books that shaped generations of programmers
Coined and popularized the term 'Web 2.0' at a 2004 conference
Organized the 1998 summit that popularized the term 'open source software'
Author of WTF?: What's the Future and Why It's Up to Us (2017)
hook: O'Reilly has spent four decades doing the same thing under different names: spotting a technology shift before the industry has language for it, then naming it. 'Open source' and 'Web 2.0' both trace to conferences he convened, and his publishing house has been the technical-literacy backbone for the programmers who built the modern internet, and now AI.

achievements.title: Founding O'Reilly Media (1978)
achievements.impact: Built the dominant technical publisher of the internet era, training generations of engineers through its books and conferences.

achievements.title: Convening the 1998 'open source' summit
achievements.impact: The meeting that coined and popularized the term 'open source software' as an alternative to 'free software,' reshaping how the industry talked about collaborative code.

achievements.title: Coining 'Web 2.0' (2004)
achievements.impact: Named and framed the shift toward user-generated, participatory web platforms, a term that defined an entire industry era.

achievements.title: WTF?: What's the Future and Why It's Up to Us (2017)
achievements.impact: Argued for a human-centered approach to technology and algorithmic platforms, prefiguring many current AI-ethics debates.

quote.text: Technology is not neutral. We're inside of what we make, and it's inside of us.
